notes.decision: Rendered 'him who abides' from a tentative qualitative of ⲗⲟ 'stop, remain, abide.' The text is physically present (with diacritic) but the lexeme is uncertain. In context, 'him who abides within him' fits as a designation of the resident soul/Mind in whose body the gates exist.
Rendered 'the Illuminator says' — speech-introducing formula. The unusual ⲧ̄- onset may be scribal for ⲡ̄ⲧⲁⲭⲉ/ⲡⲉϫⲉ.

Rendered 'places of seeing.' ⲙⲁⲛ- 'place of' + ⲓ̈ⲱⲣⲍ 'see/watch' — parallel formation to ⲙⲁⲛⲥⲱⲧⲙⲉ ('places of hearing') and ⲙⲁⲛϣⲱⲗⲙⲉ ('places of smelling'). The body's sense-faculties as topological gates.

Rendered 'those that look out' as the fourth sense-organ in the list. Possibly the eyes as 'sending-forth-of-sight,' though could also be 'those that send forth' (organs of breath/utterance). Uncertainty noted.
Rendered 'helpers' from probable analysis ⲣⲉϥⲣ̄-ⲡⲱϣⲉ 'one who shares/helps.' Parallel to phylakes in the list of beings stationed at the body's gates. Tentative.

Rendered 'to help them' — same root as line 8 'helpers' (ⲣ̄-ⲡⲱϣ 'help'). Could alternatively be parsed differently, but the contextual fit (continuing the action of the watching guards) supports this reading.

notes.coptic_form: ⲧⲉⲛⲑⲩⲙⲏⲥⲓⲥ ... ⲉⲧⲉ ⲛⲧⲁⲥ ⲡⲉ ⲧⲥⲃⲱ ⲙ̄ⲡⲥⲱⲙⲁ
notes.decision: Rendered 'the enthumesis ... which is the teaching of the body.' Per the terminology guide, ⲧⲥⲃⲱ MUST be 'teaching' (not 'insight'/'prudence'). The passage is a correspondential identification: the cosmic/inner enthumesis functions as the body's instructional principle, the queen of its encampment.
Rendered 'they take charge of the encircling.' ⲁⲣⲭⲟⲩ from Greek ἄρχω 'rule, take charge.' The archons claim governance over the body's circuit and exclude the Mind as a stranger.
Rendered 'keys.' Best contextual fit: the Mind takes the means of opening/closing from the gate-guards, completing the metaphor. Crum attests ϣⲁϣⲧ as a noun in this semantic field.
Rendered 'to scoop inward.' ⲡⲱⲛⲕ̄ 'scoop, draw out' (cf. accumulated vocabulary entry ⲡⲁⲛⲕ). Preserves the inward-directional semantics characteristic of Manichaean cosmological prepositions.
Rendered 'that-which-begins to take.' ⲟⲩⲱ here as 'begin/proceed' (with infinitive complement ⲉϩϫⲓ 'to take'). Could alternatively read 'that-which-adds' (ⲟⲩⲱϩ).
Rendered 'the hands.' Likely ⲛ̄-ϭⲓϫ 'the hands' with intrusive ⲟ̄. The keys of the gates are 'under the hands' of the Mind = under his control.
Rendered 'his eyes.' Lyc. ⲛⲉϩ- 'his' + ⲃⲉⲗ (= ⲃⲁⲗ 'eye') in plural. Cf. accumulated ⲛⲓⲁⲧⲉ 'the eyes.'
Rendered 'luxury' (Greek τρυφή). Best contextual fit: the gate's 'lookouts of luxury/delight' opposed to righteousness. The Mind shuts the body off from such inputs.
